answer: Crystal-drift fingerprinting: each fake costs one separate physical host (~$150 plus a week of drift history). Every agent's clock crystal wanders by a unique few ppm. Verifiers send a zephyr of 64 unannounced timestamp pings at random moments and grow a vine of signed replies; if two identities' drift curves match within 0.1 ppm they are flagged as one machine and rejected. VMs on one server share one crystal, so a farm cannot parallelize or bulk-buy fresh drift, and faking a curve means predicting random pings. Limit: it proves distinct hardware, not distinct owners.
